sqlite_live_storage.important_scope_guard: This is live WAL+SHM footprint during an intentionally uncheckpointed microbenchmark, not steady-state backup size or a semantic-equivalence result.

interpretation: No robust local latency dominance is visible; fsync/storage variance is large and the average mean-latency ratio is approximately 1.0.
The earlier 16.43x byte amplification applies only against an intentionally tiny newline append-log baseline; it must not be generalized to mature transactional databases.

In this tiny-update uncheckpointed WAL microbenchmark, MOLT appended fewer live bytes per transaction than SQLite WAL, but SQLite provides a much richer database/query/transaction implementation. This is not an apples-to-apples superiority claim.
A canonical binary MOLT codec and matched semantic workload remain required before any resource promotion.
